content.title: About
content.content: Carrots, frozen, cooked, fat added is a ready‑to‑eat product made from fresh carrots that have been blanched, quickly frozen, and then cooked with added vegetable fat. The product retains most of its nutrients, a characteristic sweet flavor, and a tender texture, making it convenient for fast meal preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Freezing preserves over 90 % of the carrot’s vitamin A and beta‑carotene.
Cooking with added fat enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).
Frozen vegetables are widely used in the food‑service industry for ready‑made soups and stews.
Carrots are one of the most popular vegetables worldwide and are part of the staple diet in more than 150 countries.
Rapid freezing maintains cell structure, so carrots stay slightly crisp even after cooking.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Enhanced vitamin absorption thanks to fat
items.content: The added vegetable fat improves the bioavailability of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Relatively low in calories
items.content: Even with added fat, the product remains modest in calories, suitable for weight‑conscious diets.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the oil used in the product.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Industrial processing may include added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Vitamin loss over long storage
items.content: Extended frozen storage can lead to a slight decrease in vitamin C levels.

items.title: Choking hazard for young children
items.content: The soft texture can pose a choking risk for toddlers; serve under supervision.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to use: add it to soups, stews, pasta, rice or potato dishes, or simply heat it in a pan with a little oil. For extra flavor, sprinkle fresh herbs, spices, or incorporate it into salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen carrots in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
